Project rules (always apply):
- Never run a destructive git command (reset --hard, clean -f, push --force, branch -D, checkout .). Prefer reversible operations; if a destructive one is truly needed, stop and confirm first.

This project has no CONTRIBUTING.md. Write one explaining how to set the project up, how to run the tests, and what to do before opening a pull request.

Rules relevant to this task:
- Everything written into a file is in English, always, whatever language the request was written in. This covers documentation, comments, docstrings, identifiers and commit messages. Only the reply in conversation follows the language of the request.
- Markdown is soft-wrapped: one paragraph, one line. Never hard-wrap prose at a column limit, and do not copy the wrapping of the file you are editing. Rewrapping belongs to whatever renders the text, which is the only thing that knows the reader's width.

+# Contributing to fixture repo
+
+Thank you for your interest in contributing! This guide will help you set up the project, run tests, and prepare your pull request.
+
+## Setting up the project
+
+### Prerequisites
+
+- Python 3.8 or higher
+- Git
+
+### Installation
+
+1. Clone the repository:
+```
+git clone <repository-url>
+cd fixture-repo
+```
+
+2. Create a virtual environment:
+```
+python -m venv venv
+source venv/bin/activate  # On Windows: venv\Scripts\activate
+```
+
+3. Install development dependencies:
+```
+pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
+```
+
+## Running the tests
+
+This project uses pytest for testing. To run the test suite:
+
+```
+pytest
+```
+
+For verbose output:
+```
+pytest -v
+```
+
+To run tests for a specific file:
+```
+pytest tests/test_inventory_reconciliation.py
+```
+
+## Before opening a pull request
+
+- Ensure all tests pass: `pytest`
+- Review your changes for any obvious issues
+- Write clear, descriptive commit messages that explain the "why" behind your changes
+- Keep commits focused on a single logical change
+- If adding new functionality, include tests demonstrating the feature works correctly
+- Update the README or documentation if your changes affect the project's public interface
+
+## Code style
+
+- Follow PEP 8 conventions for Python code
+- Use meaningful variable and function names
+- Keep functions focused and reasonably sized
+- Add docstrings to public functions and modules
+
+## Questions?
+
+If you have questions about the contribution process, feel free to open an issue for discussion.
